To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we identified a mouse mutant that has the same symptoms as human primary ciliary dyskenesia (PCD); (2) this mutation is in a gene that encodes a protein that is part of the outer dynein arms of the cilia; (3) the mutant mouse has a defect in cilia function, as shown by the immotility of cilia in the airway;

we have identified the first mutation in a dynein heavy-chain gene (DNAH5) in patients with PCD, and we have shown that this mutation is responsible for a severe form of PCD that includes hydrocephalus.
we have characterized a mouse mutation that reproduces most features of human primary ciliary dyskinnesia (PCD).
In summary, our research is concerned with
a mouse model of PCD.
a better understanding of the genetic basis of PCD and the pathogenesis of hydrocephalus.
understanding the function and regulation of the dyneins and other microtubule motors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
mutations in Mdh5 are a primary genetic cause of PCD.
mutations in Mdhah5 are responsible for the development of primary ciliary dyskinetic syndrome.
mutations in DNAH5 can cause PCD with or without hydrocephalus.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we show that a mutation in the Mdnah5 gene causes a syndrome of PCD, situs inversis and hydrocephalus in mice, and this mutation is homologous to a mutation in the DNAH5 gene in human PCD patients.
mutations in DNAH5 are the most common cause of human PCD and are also associated with the development of hydrocephalus.
mutations in the dynein gene Mdnah5 cause primary ciliary dyskinensia (PCD) and hydrocephalus in mice, and mutations in human DNAH5 cause PCD in humans.
The main takeaway from our work is that
mutations in axonemal heavy chain dynein genes are a cause of PCD in mice and humans.
the mouse model of PCD is a valuable tool to study the molecular basis of the human disease.
Mdnah5 is a primary gene for PCD in humans and that mutations in DNAH5 are the cause of PCD in the patients.
